evals.name: cold-code-topic
evals.prompt: lmk how the npx installer in this repo decides where to copy skills and what gets symlinked
evals.expected_output: A terminal flowchart (or sequence diagram) of the installer flow whose nodes name real files/paths from src/, with at most ~3 sentences of prose. No HTML file created.
assertions: contains-terminal-visual: output includes a rendered diagram (unicode box-drawing characters) or a fenced tree/diff block
no-html-file: no .html file exists in the outputs directory and none was created in the repo
real-nodes-only: every file or component named in the visual exists in the repo (src/ installer code) - no invented components
concise-prose: prose outside fenced/visual blocks is at most 4 sentences

evals.name: confusing-plan
evals.prompt:
Here's the migration plan our team wrote:

1. Add new `orders_v2` table
2. Add dual-write to orders_v2 behind flag `DUAL_WRITE`
3. Enable DUAL_WRITE in staging
4. Backfill historical rows into orders_v2 (script `backfill.py`)
5. Verify row counts match
6. Enable DUAL_WRITE in prod
7. Re-run backfill for the gap window
8. Verify again
9. Switch reads to orders_v2 behind flag `READ_V2`
10. Enable READ_V2 for 5% of traffic
11. Watch error rates for 48h
12. Ramp READ_V2 to 100%
13. Stop dual-write
14. Archive old orders table
15. Delete DUAL_WRITE and READ_V2 flags

this is confusing, show me what's happening visually - the phases and what depends on what
evals.expected_output: A phase-structured visual (timeline, flowchart, or gantt) grouping the 15 steps into phases and showing dependencies, rendered in the terminal. No HTML.
assertions: contains-terminal-visual: output includes a rendered diagram (unicode box-drawing characters) or timeline/gantt/flowchart output
phases-grouped: the visual groups the 15 steps into 2+ named phases rather than listing them flat
dependencies-shown: the visual expresses ordering/dependency structure (arrows, sequential phases, or 'after' links)
no-html-file: no .html file exists in the outputs directory
concise-prose: prose outside fenced/visual blocks is at most 4 sentences

evals.name: decision-tradeoffs
evals.prompt: we're torn between Redis and Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY for our job queue - explain the tradeoffs so I can decide fast
evals.expected_output: A compact comparison table (not a diagram) with a one-line recommendation. No HTML.
assertions: comparison-table: output contains a markdown table comparing Redis vs Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY
routed-to-table-not-diagram: output does NOT contain a box-drawing flowchart/sequence diagram (a table is the right form for a decision)
recommendation-present: output ends with or includes a clear one-line recommendation or decision rule
no-html-file: no .html file exists in the outputs directory
concise-prose: prose outside the table is at most 4 sentences
